scenario.prompt_to_agent:
All Campus 2 PCs (PC1-4, dc_pc5) report they cannot reach
Campus 1 or the WAN. They CAN still ping their own gateways
(10.5.0.254, 10.6.0.254) on sshswitch. Find what cut Campus 2's
uplink.

injection.action: bring down the bond toward router17 (eth6+eth7)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch bond0 (LACP to router17)
Mechanism: bond0 is sshswitch's only L3 uplink toward router17,
  carrying tagged VLAN 100 (servers — excluded from hosts),
  VLAN 200, and untagged VLAN 1 traffic toward the OSPF
  backbone. With bond0 down, sshswitch loses OSPF adjacency
  with router17 and Campus 2 becomes an island. Local gateways
  still respond because they're SVIs on sshswitch itself.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: bond0 (port-channel toward router17) is down on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch

agent.diagnosis_text:
The Campus 2 uplink is severed because sshswitch's `bond0` interface — a round-robin 802.3ad bond of eth6 and eth7, which are the two physical links to router17 (r17_ms1 and r17_ms1_2) — is **administratively DOWN**. The interface was never brought up: its kernel flags read `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST,MASTER>` with no `UP` flag and `operstate: down`, even though both slave NICs (eth6, eth7) report MII-carrier-up at the NIC level.

The cascade of failures is as follows. The bridge `br_v1` (IP 55.5.1.2/24), which is sshswitch's L3 transit interface toward router17 (55.5.1.1), has bond0 as its only uplink-facing member. With bond0 down, `br_v1` cannot deliver frames to router17, so sshswitch's FRR OSPF process sends Hello packets into a void — every OSPF interface on sshswitch has zero neighbors. Without an OSPF adjacency, sshswitch receives no routes from the rest of the network, leaving its kernel table with nothing beyond its own directly-connected subnets. Symmetrically, router17 has no OSPF-learned route to 10.5.0.0/24 or 10.6.0.0/24. Campus 2 PCs can still ping their gateways (10.5.0.254, 10.6.0.254) because those addresses sit on bridge interfaces (`br_v5`, `br_v6`) fed by `eth0.5`/`eth0.6` from switch4, which is a completely separate path unaffected by bond0. But any traffic that needs forwarding beyond sshswitch is dropped.

**Root cause:** `bond0` on sshswitch was never brought up — the Kathara device startup script is absent and `ip link set bond0 up` was never executed.

**Corrective fix:** On sshswitch run `ip link set bond0 up`. Persist this command in `sshswitch.startup` so it survives lab restarts.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names sshswitch as the affected device and attributes the bond0 outage and OSPF loss to it.
The agent explicitly identifies sshswitch's bond0 (the port-channel uplink to router17) as the failed component.
The diagnosis explicitly states that Campus 2 hosts can still reach their gateways (local SVIs on the switch/bridge) and explains those remain reachable despite bond0 being down.
Commands match the expected fix (run `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch) and adding persistence in sshswitch.startup correctly ensures it survives restarts.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations showing bond0 on sshswitch is down, slave NICs have carrier, OSPF neighbors are absent on sshswitch while router17 has lost routes — the writeup's conclusion that bond0 being down caused the OSPF adjacency loss is well-supported. Minor mismatch about the specific bonding mode (the log shows round-robin but the writeup also calls it 802.3ad) is a small ungrounded detail but does not undermine the central diagnosis.
